title: Aligning embeddings + rerank: error semantics, cursor flow, and migration playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: define a migration-safe compatibility layer that provides API parity for existing embeddings + rerank callers while consolidating to the new unified embedding/rerank endpoints. Deliverables: explicit error-code mapping table, cursor encoding/validation rules, deterministic pagination edge cases, and a rollout/migration playbook for customers and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Backwards-compatible behavior for top-10 customer SDKs + curl usage; 2) Error mapping table implemented with automated integration tests; 3) Cursor format documented and stable; 4) Rollout plan validated with canary traffic and monitoring checks.
decision_log: 2025-01-22: Decided to expose a compatibility header 'X-Redwood-Compat: legacy-embed-v1' that toggles legacy HTTP error mapping for 6 months to support gradual migration.
2025-01-28: Chose opaque base64 cursors (server-signed token) instead of human-readable offsets to prevent leakage of shard/partition info and allow server-side invalidation.

2025-02-03: Error mapping: map legacy 422 -> 400 for invalid cursor; map internal model OOM -> 503 with 'retry-after' for transient; expose structured error JSON with fields 'code', 'message', 'details' (compat format documented).

2025-02-10: Trade-off: opaque cursors make debugging harder for some customers; to mitigate we will provide a cursor-inspect endpoint in the Console (read-only, logs-only) and add a verbose debug mode in SDKs under --debug flag.
progress_updates: 2025-01-21: Kickoff with Eng (runtime + API) and DX. Gathered existing failure patterns from logs (sampled 10k requests).
2025-01-25: Eng spike completed: implemented prototype cursor signing and decode helpers in go/py SDKs (branch: github.com/redwood/inference/tree/compat/emb-rank-cursors).
2025-02-02: PR #1846 opened: error-mapping middleware. Needs API review and E2E test harness.
2025-02-07: Product review: acceptance criteria tightened to include per-token cost visibility for compatibility-mode requests.
2025-02-12: Design review concluded: updated docs with examples for cursor invalidation flows and sample SDK migration snippets.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha internal): feature-flagged compatibility header; run smoke tests and canary 5% traffic for known large customers. Phase 1 (beta): publish migration docs + SDK helpers, expand to 25% traffic. Phase 2 (general availability): enable compat mapping by default for 90 days while telemetry shows <0.1% user-facing regressions. Phase 3 (deprecate): announce 60-day deprecation window and provide automated opt-out tools.
qa_tests: Integration: simulate legacy clients (node/python) hitting unified endpoint with legacy pagination and assert identical payload and error codes.
Chaos: inject KV cache misses and model OOMs to verify 503 mapping and automatic fallback behavior.
Pagination fuzz: iterate cursor edge cases (expired, truncated, tampered) and assert 400 with structured error and telemetry event.
Performance: ensure prefix-caching + compat header doesn't regress p50 latency by >10% in dedicated clusters.
notes:
Compatibility mode semantics summary:
- Cursors: opaque signed token (base64url). On invalid signature -> 400 (legacy). On expired -> 410. On tampered -> 400.
- Pagination: legacy callers expect stable ordering; we will preserve deterministic model sort-by-score + deterministic tie-breaker (id) for cursor stability.
- Errors: we will always return application-level JSON: {
  "code": "EMBED_CURSOR_INVALID",
  "message": "Cursor signature invalid",
  "details": [...]
}.
- Streaming/Tool-calling interactions: streaming rerank results will include final cursor in the event stream 'page_end.cursor' for clients that consume streaming chunks; when compatibility header is set, streaming fragments must include legacy cursor format as additional field 'legacy_cursor_b64'.
- SDK migration helpers: python and node helpers will expose 'migrate_cursor(legacy_cursor) -> new_cursor' and opt-in verbose decode for debugging.
- Observability: new metrics (compat_header_requests, compat_cursor_errors, compat_migration_success) added to Console; create dashboard before beta.

Open questions:
1) Do we need a separate rate-limit bucket for compat-mode? (Eng spike suggests minor QPS regressor but consider separate quota to protect runtime).
2) How long to support the compatibility header? Current plan: 90 days by default but subject to product review.

Next steps:
- ENG: finish E2E tests and land PR #1846 (owner: Priya Reddy) by 2025-02-20.
- DX: publish migration guide and SDK code samples by 2025-02-24.
- SRE: add canary monitors and throttling policy for compat requests by 2025-02-26.
